method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited texts with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a seat-neutral core (mva-core.l4) with five regulative rules (s 126A(1) with reg 4(1)(b); s 127(2)(b); s 127(2)(c); s 126A(4); s 124AB(1) with its 95% rate), run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; two seat layers (the claimant; the insured owner or driver) that restate no rule; answers are named outcomes, no MAYBE BOOLEAN, so no NOTHING-kind tags; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Both from the Open Australian Legal Corpus (South Australian legislation last collected 2025-03-10), not the official texts, and possibly out of date: Motor Vehicles Act 1959, corpus document south_australian_legislation:2024-11-07/1959.53.un, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/motor-vehicles-act-1959.txt (sha256 507991172d1f665b606d4d086c1a68c7e659dab8f8e9cbccd197585c78019a6e); Motor Vehicles (Third Party Insurance) Regulations 2013, corpus document south_australian_legislation:2021-11-01/2013.164.un, as deposited at subjects/au/sa/motor-vehicles-third-party-insurance-regulations-2013/registers/source-bundle/motor-vehicles-third-party-insurance-regulations-2013.txt (sha256 188bd0735e549c7fa936eee7abc472fb01d243453877e77101762a514e7b022f), regs 4-6 quoted in mva-core.l4. Accidents on or after 1 July 2013 only. CPI figures, the CTP Regulator's policy terms and the Magistrates Court scale are inputs or named in answers.

seats: the claimant: the person injured in a motor accident, or the person claiming for a death, bringing a compulsory third party claim under Part 4 (mva-seat.l4)
the insured owner or driver against whom a claim is made, including the driver of an uninsured vehicle facing the nominal defendant (mva-seat-insured.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run mva-dates.l4 ; l4 run mva-core.l4 ; l4 run mva-seat.l4 ; l4 run mva-seat-insured.l4 ; l4 run mva-cases.l4 ; l4 run mva-cases-insured.l4
checks.result: 193 assertions written, 193 satisfied (131 + 62), 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07); 3 #TRACEs with an expect line, each as expected; a negative control (30 days of grace to 31, the $25 000 costs line to $25 001) failed exactly the 2 predicted assertions and was reverted
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: In: Motor Vehicles Act 1959 Part 4: s 99(1), (3), (3a), (4); s 99A(8), (10), (17), (19) with s 109; s 104(1)(a), (2); ss 112, 113 (s 117 noted), 113A, 114; s 115(1), (3), (4); s 116(1)-(5), (7)-(7e); s 118A(3); s 118B (applied); s 123; s 124(1)-(6b); s 124A(1)-(4); ss 124AB, 124AC, 126, 126A; s 127(2), (6), (6a), (7); s 127B(2)-(4); ss 127C, 133, 134. Third Party Insurance Regulations 2013 regs 4-6. Out: premiums, approved insurers and policy machinery (s 99A otherwise, ss 101, 105, 107, 116A, 119-122, 128, 129A, 131); s 102 (the uninsured driving offence); ss 110, 111, 111A (payments to practitioners, hospitals, the Treasurer); s 124AA (foreign awards); ss 125, 125A, 125B (insurer's conduct of the defence); s 127A (medical charges); s 132 (disqualification); s 104(1)(b) policy terms (not deposited); the Civil Liability Act 1936 and the Lifetime Support Scheme Act 2013 (other subjects). Reasons in NOTES.md.
